## The reaction list and its rate-parameter keys (`reactions`) {#sec-ch11-yaml-reactions}

### Summary

The `reactions` block is a YAML list; each entry is one reaction with an `equation`, a `type` and a
`rate-constant` map. Each rate form has its own reader, and each reader walks the whole list and keeps only the
entries whose `type` matches its own name. This section lists the types, the keys each reader takes, and the value
each key gets when it is left out. The rate laws themselves are @sec-ch06's subject.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Turn the `reactions` list into one options object per rate form.

**Data.** `equation`, `type`, `rate-constant` keys; units as stated per key.

**Placement.** Inside `KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml`, after the species registry is filled.

**Activation.** Present `reactions` key; without it the options carry no reactions.

**Guarantee / limits.** Several keys default silently; see Limits.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Every entry needs a `type`: the Arrhenius and nucleation readers refuse an entry without one. A type no reader
claims is skipped without a message.

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme parses input. Unit conversion of the pre-exponential factor is the one computation:
`A` is read in the unit system molecule, cm, s and converted to mol, m, s, with the exponent set by the sum of
the reactant stoichiometric coefficients ({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
The conversion itself is not re-derived in this draft.

### Numerical method

No numerical method and no figure: the scheme is a parser. `KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics_options.cpp KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}) calls the readers in this order,
each on the whole list:

1. Arrhenius (`type: arrhenius`);
2. coagulation (`type: coagulation`), which reuses the Arrhenius reader;
3. evaporation (`type: evaporation`);
4. three-body (`type: three-body`);
5. Lindemann fall-off (`type: falloff` with neither a `Troe` nor an `SRI` key);
6. Troe fall-off (`type: falloff` with `Troe`);
7. SRI fall-off (`type: falloff` with `SRI`).

It then registers every species the reactions name as a vapor or a cloud, refuses a vapor the `species` list does
not hold, sorts both id lists, and copies each registered species' reference constants and NASA-9 coefficients
into the options.

#### Arrhenius and coagulation

`ArrheniusOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}})
requires `equation` and `rate-constant` and reads, inside `rate-constant`:

- `A`: default $1$ when absent, in internal units; when present it is converted as stated in the Derivation layer.
- `b`: default $0$.
- `Ea_R` [K]: default $1$, not $0$. A reaction written without `Ea_R` therefore gets the factor
  $\exp(-1\,\mathrm{K}/T)$, not $1$. The key `Ea` is not read by this reader.
- `E4`: default $0$, stored as `E4_R`. `ArrheniusImpl::reset`
  ({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusImpl::reset >}}) registers it as a buffer, but
  `ArrheniusImpl::forward` ({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusImpl::forward >}}) never reads it: the
  value is parsed and has no effect on the rate.
- `p-threshold` [Pa] and `factor`: both or neither; `p-threshold` must be finite and $> 0$, `factor` finite and
  $\ge 0$.
- `A_ranges` with `T_ranges` (same length, required together), and optionally `b_ranges` and `Ea_R_ranges` (same
  length; each defaults to zeros, not to the single-range `b` and `Ea_R`).

Coagulation entries are read by the same function under the name `coagulation`.

#### Fall-off and three-body

The three fall-off readers take `low-P-rate-constant` and `high-P-rate-constant`, both required, an optional
`efficiencies` map, and the `Troe` or `SRI` map that selects the form. The three-body reader takes one
`rate-constant` map and an optional `efficiencies` map. Each rate map is read by a file-local
`parse_arrhenius_params`; the fall-off one is `parse_arrhenius_params`
({{< code src/kinetics/lindemann_falloff.cpp parse_arrhenius_params >}}), and the three-body reader carries a copy
with the same rules ({{< code src/kinetics/three_body.cpp parse_arrhenius_params >}}). Their defaults differ from
the Arrhenius reader: `Ea_R` is used when present, else `Ea` is read as a number followed by an optional unit word (a word
containing `cal` divides by $1.987$, `kJ` multiplies by $1000/8.314$, `J` divides by $8.314$, no word is taken
as kelvin), and with neither key the activation temperature is $0$.

#### Nucleation and evaporation

`NucleationOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/thermo/nucleation.cpp NucleationOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}})
requires `formula` (the saturation vapour pressure function) and reads `minT` (default $0\,\mathrm{K}$) and
`maxT` (default $10^4\,\mathrm{K}$). `EvaporationOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp EvaporationOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) first calls the nucleation reader on
the same list, then reads, per evaporation entry:

- `form`: `diffusion` (default) or `kessler`; anything else is refused.
- `k3`: required for `kessler`, refused otherwise; finite and $\ge 0$.
- `diff_c` (default $2\times10^{-5}$), `diff_T` (default $1.75$), `diff_P` (default $-1$), `vm` (default
  $1.8\times10^{-5}$), `diameter` (default $10^{-2}$); with `form: kessler` each of these is refused.
- `minT` and `maxT` again, with the same defaults.

Because the nucleation reader has already pushed `minT` and `maxT` for each evaporation entry, the evaporation
options end with two entries per reaction in `minT` and in `maxT`, while `reactions` has one. No code at the pin
reads `minT()` or `maxT()` outside the two readers and the options' `report`, so this is read from the code as
having no effect on rates; that is a hypothesis, not tested.

The reactions block of the test card {{< code tests/earth.yaml >}}:

```yaml
reactions:
  - equation: H2O <=> H2O(l)
    type: nucleation
    rate-constant: {formula: h2o_ideal}

  - equation: H2O(l) => H2O(l,p)
    type: coagulation
    rate-constant: {A: 0.01, b: 0, Ea_R: 0.}

  - equation: H2O(l,p) => H2O
    type: evaporation
    rate-constant: {formula: h2o_ideal, diff_c: 0.2e-4, diff_T: 1.75, diff_P: -1., vm: 18.e-6, diameter: 1.0e-4}
```

The coagulation entry sets `Ea_R: 0.` explicitly; left out, it would be $1\,\mathrm{K}$.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `Ea_R` defaults to $1\,\mathrm{K}$ in the Arrhenius and coagulation readers, and to $0$ in the fall-off and
  three-body readers.
- `E4` is accepted and stored but does not enter the Arrhenius rate.
- Evaporation entries store `minT` and `maxT` twice per reaction.
- The Arrhenius reader ignores `Ea`; the fall-off and three-body readers accept it.
- `type: kb-falloff` has no YAML reader: `KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml` reads no KB fall-off entries. The
  options are filled by the KINETICS-base `.pun` reader of @sec-ch06, or by hand (see below).
- A `type` no reader claims is dropped without a message.
:::

By hand, KB fall-off options are set through the `kb_falloff` field of `KineticsOptionsImpl`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsOptionsImpl >}}). In Python, `bind_kinetics`
({{< code python/csrc/pykinetics.cpp bind_kinetics >}}) exposes the class `KBFalloffOptions`, with setters for
`Tref`, `fc`, `units`, `reactions`, `k0_A`, `k0_b`, `k0_Ea_R`, `kinf_A`, `kinf_b` and `kinf_Ea_R`, and the setter
`KineticsOptions.kb_falloff`. The one reader that fills the field is `kinetics_options_from_kinetics_base_pun`
({{< code src/photochem/kinetics_base_reader.cpp kinetics_options_from_kinetics_base_pun >}}).

The older reader `parse_reactions_yaml` ({{< code src/utils/parse_yaml.cpp parse_reactions_yaml overload=1 >}}) defaults
`type` to `arrhenius` and prints a message for `three-body` and `falloff` instead of building them; its C++ test
is not registered in `ctest`. Which callers still use it is not checked in this draft.
